But the error message is `imp: .imp/ already exists at /path/to/parent/.imp` which might surprise a user who thought they were in a fresh dir. Minor.

expected_findings.description: _split_providers silently drops unknown tokens without feedback; if a user types 'anthropic googleai', the function returns ['anthropic'] without warning about the dropped 'googleai' entry.
_build_role_map emits a top-level providers: block that load_config ignores entirely, creating dead output in the generated YAML.
The .gitignore substring check using `if l not in existing` is fragile; it will match partial lines like comments, potentially skipping the append if a pre-existing comment mentions the entry.
The test only verifies that some role has some openai entry; it should also verify every role has openai in its prefer list and that anthropic is first to confirm input ordering is preserved.
There is no test for the silent-drop code path in _split_providers, such as testing that 'anthropic googleai' produces a warning.
The output line `Try: imp new "Your first change"` uses double quotes that will be emitted verbatim by print, not interpreted as shell quoting; this is acceptable with no escaping issue.

Model names like claude-opus-4-7, claude-sonnet-4-6, and gpt-5 appear consistent with production but are speculative; a TODO comment noting verification against OpenAI's current model catalog would be prudent.

When called from a subdirectory of an already-initialized project, the error message will reference the parent .imp/ directory, which is confusing; a more informative error message about finding existing .imp/ in a parent directory would improve UX.
